label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences, gated by first token (j,s,y,r,n,e,z,...)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively (98% of activations, 99% of mass) at the delimiter step, i.e. when the model must output the first original token. Within that step it depends strongly on sequence length: rate is about 0% for L<=6, 3% at L=7, 26% at L=8, 45% at L=9 (L>=8 holds 95% of mass). It is further modulated by the first original token (the token about to be output): j, s, y, r, n, e, z, k, b, h, g, 1 give the highest rates; first tokens such as a, c, d, i, l give few activations. The strongest activations (top quartile, 85% covered) are L=9 sequences starting with j/s/y/n. A small residue (about 1% of mass) fires on the last original-phase step (t=7 or 8 of L=9) on inputs d/o/u just before <DEL>. Never fires in the copy phase or at early original steps. The predicate (delimiter, L>=8, first token in the favored set) gets F1 about 0.66 on dev; the first-token dependence is graded rather than a clean set, so precision and recall are both incomplete.
